source_span: Capital hasn't disappeared. It's become far more discriminating... the market is increasingly differentiating between companies that can finance growth and those whose growth depends on financing remaining available.
source_chain: AI-linked credit (CoreWeave, Oracle, neoclouds) sold off hard this week while the broad IG index barely moved (~2bps) therefore capital is not fleeing credit but discriminating within it therefore the market is pricing issuers by whether they can self-fund growth versus depend on financing staying open, with CCC/HY already showing the damage (15.4% yields, 1,045bps spreads) — invalidation/escalation flagged by Academy Securities: the widening has been orderly so far but dealers pulling back from two-week-old new issues is a liquidity warning sign that the move turns 'fast and furious' (10-20bps IG, 3-5pts HY), a bigger risk than a move tighter.
pulse_chain: AI/hyperscaler credit spreads hit their widest of the year (CoreWeave 15% yields, Oracle +43bps to 320, Meta +14bps, CDS +30-40bps) while the broad IG index moved only ~2bps therefore this is a sorting, not a retreat: capital still wants credit risk but is now pricing an issuer's ability to finance its own growth against dependence on financing staying open (AA+ hyperscalers insulated per Morgan Stanley, neoclouds and CCC/HY most exposed) therefore Academy Securities (yellow-to-orange alert) expects the orderly widening to turn fast and furious (10-20bps IG, 3-5pts HY, a bigger risk than tightening), with dealers already pulling back from two-week-old issues — invalidation/catalyst: CoreWeave testing its July lows is the thing to watch, even as distressed/equity buyers were already stepping into its debt late in the week.
why: The pulse reproduces GS Pasi's discriminating-not-fleeing mechanism verbatim in substance, correctly attributes the AA-hyperscaler/interest-coverage point to Morgan Stanley and the alert escalation/liquidity-warning/bp sizing to Academy Securities, and keeps Academy's own invalidation condition (CoreWeave's price action) as the forward-looking tell.
